**SECTION A: DATABASE (Nina's Shop)** *(20 marks)*

The relation **R** below keeps records of customers and the items they buy from Nina's shop.

| CustomerID | CustomerName | ItemCode | ItemName | UnitPrice | Quantity | TotalPrice | TDate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C001 | Ebai Paul | IT001 | Rice | 200 | 3 | 600 | 09/09/2021 |
| C001 | Ebai Paul | IT002 | Beans | 250 | 2 | 500 | 09/09/2021 |
| C001 | Ebai Paul | IT003 | Corn | 175 | 2 | 350 | 10/10/2021 |
| C002 | Eyere Esther | IT003 | Corn | 175 | 5 | 875 | 11/12/2021 |

Relation **R** has the following attributes with names of obvious meanings; the primary key field is underlined:

`R(`<u>`CustomerID`</u>`, CustomerName, ItemCode, ItemName, UnitPrice, Quantity, TotalPrice, TDate)`
incertitudes: Relation R : le sujet imprime « the primary key field is underlined » et ne souligne que CustomerID. Cet attribut ne peut pas être une clé, car C001 apparaît trois fois ; recopié tel quel, écart signalé dans le corrigé (la clé de R est (CustomerID, ItemCode, TDate)).

Points : Task 1 = 6 imprimé. Les barèmes imprimés dans (i) sont 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, donc points = 4 pour (i) ; aucun point n'est imprimé pour (ii) (les 2 points restants sont déduits, non imprimés) : points = null pour (ii). Aucun point corrigé.

Dates de R lues en jour/mois/année (convention du Cameroun) : « 11/12/2021 » est lu 11 décembre 2021, ce que le sujet ne précise pas ; 09/09/2021 et 10/10/2021 sont sans ambiguïté. Le corrigé stocke les dates au format AAAA-MM-JJ.

Aucun corrigé officiel : le corrigé est rédigé. Le choix de la clé de Customer_Item (CustomerID, ItemCode, TDate) et de garder TotalPrice comme montant facturé est un choix de conception, expliqué dans le corrigé, qui accepte aussi la clé minimale (CustomerID, ItemCode).

La décomposition a été vérifiée avec sqlite3 (module Python) : la jointure des trois relations redonne exactement les quatre lignes de R. Le schéma attendu en (ii) est un diagramme à compléter (trois cadres vides imprimés, aucune figure indispensable) : il est décrit dans le corrigé sous forme de diagramme en texte, sans PNG.
Le sujet est un scan avec des filigranes et des publicités (gcerevision.com, kawlo), ignorés. Cases à remplir en pointillés non transcrites (remplacées par des points de suspension).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Task 1: Database Design** *(6 marks)*

(i) In a fully normalised relational database the data in the relation **R** is stored in the relations: `Customer`, `Item`, and `Customer_Item`. `Customer_Item` holds details about items bought by customers. Complete each of these relations making sure that their primary key attribute(s) is /are underlined.

`Customer(` ............................................ `)` *[1 mark]*

`Item(` ............................................ `)` *[1 mark]*

`Customer_Item(` ............................................ `)` *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Step 1 - Find the dependencies in R.** Reading the data of R (and the meaning of the attributes):

- `CustomerID -> CustomerName` (a customer has one name);
- `ItemCode -> ItemName, UnitPrice` (an item has one name and one unit price);
- `(CustomerID, ItemCode, TDate) -> Quantity, TotalPrice` (what was bought, how many, and the amount paid, on a given date), with `TotalPrice = UnitPrice x Quantity`.

*Remark on the printed statement.* The booklet underlines only `CustomerID` as the primary key of R. That cannot be a key, because the value C001 appears in three rows; the real key of R is `(CustomerID, ItemCode, TDate)`. The printed key is not used below.

R is not even in second normal form: `CustomerName` depends on a part of the key only (`CustomerID`), and `ItemName`, `UnitPrice` depend on a part only (`ItemCode`). The consequences are the usual anomalies: "Ebai Paul" is written three times and "Corn, 175" twice (update anomaly), a new item that nobody has bought yet cannot be stored (insertion anomaly), and deleting the only purchase of an item loses the item itself (deletion anomaly).

**Step 2 - Split R so that every attribute depends on the key, the whole key and nothing but the key.** Primary keys are underlined.

`Customer(`<u>`CustomerID`</u>`, CustomerName)` *(1 mark)*

`Item(`<u>`ItemCode`</u>`, ItemName, UnitPrice)` *(1 mark)*

`Customer_Item(`<u>`CustomerID`</u>`,` <u>`ItemCode`</u>`,` <u>`TDate`</u>`, Quantity, TotalPrice)` *(2 marks)*

In `Customer_Item`, `CustomerID` is also a **foreign key** referencing `Customer`, and `ItemCode` a foreign key referencing `Item`.

**Step 3 - Justify the choices.**

- `Customer` and `Item` have a single-attribute key and all other attributes depend on it alone: 2NF and 3NF.
- `Customer_Item` records one purchase line, so its key must identify one line. `(CustomerID, ItemCode)` is enough for the four rows printed (and is the minimum answer that a marker will accept), but the same customer can buy the same item again on another day; adding `TDate` to the key makes the design valid for future data. `Quantity` and `TotalPrice` depend on the whole key; `TDate` is a key attribute, so there is no partial dependency.
- `TotalPrice` is derivable (`UnitPrice x Quantity`), yet it is **kept in `Customer_Item` on purpose**: it is the amount charged at the time of the sale. If the unit price of an item changes later (Task 3(ii)), the old purchases must keep their old amount; recomputing them from the current `UnitPrice` would falsify the history. A purist 3NF design that always recomputes the total is also acceptable if the answer says so.

**Check.** The three relations were created in SQLite and filled with the data of R; joining them back (`Customer_Item` with `Customer` and `Item`) gives exactly the four rows of R, so the decomposition loses no information and repeats no fact.

**Marking:** `Customer` with its key underlined (1); `Item` with its key underlined (1); `Customer_Item` with the composite key underlined (1) and the remaining attributes `Quantity`, `TotalPrice`, `TDate` placed correctly (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Complete the entity-relationship diagram below for the entities `Customer`, `Item` and `Customer_Item`.

*(The booklet prints three empty boxes: `Customer` at the top left, `Item` at the top right, and `Customer_Item` below them, in the middle.)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the relationships.** One customer can have many purchase lines, and each line belongs to one customer: **one-to-many** (1:N) from `Customer` to `Customer_Item`. One item can appear in many purchase lines, and each line concerns one item: **one-to-many** (1:N) from `Item` to `Customer_Item`. Together, `Customer` and `Item` are in a **many-to-many** relationship (a customer buys many items, an item is bought by many customers), which is resolved by the associative entity `Customer_Item`.

**Completed diagram** (PK = primary key, to be underlined in the booklet; FK = foreign key; the "1" and "N" are the cardinalities written at the ends of each line):

```
 +------------------+                         +------------------+
 | Customer         |                         | Item             |
 |------------------|                         |------------------|
 | CustomerID  (PK) |                         | ItemCode   (PK)  |
 | CustomerName     |                         | ItemName         |
 +------------------+                         | UnitPrice        |
          | 1                                 +------------------+
          |                                            | 1
        buys                                       is sold in
          |                                            |
          | N                                          | N
          |       +-------------------------+          |
          +-------| Customer_Item           |----------+
                  |-------------------------|
                  | CustomerID  (PK, FK)    |
                  | ItemCode    (PK, FK)    |
                  | TDate       (PK)        |
                  | Quantity                |
                  | TotalPrice              |
                  +-------------------------+
```

The foreign keys `CustomerID` and `ItemCode` in `Customer_Item` are what the two lines represent in the relational schema.

**Marking** (the booklet prints no mark for this part; the 2 marks left in Task 1 are assumed to belong to it): a line from `Customer` to `Customer_Item` and a line from `Item` to `Customer_Item`, with no line directly between `Customer` and `Item` (1); the 1:N cardinalities written on the correct sides, the "many" end at `Customer_Item` (1).
